title: Variadic functions and stdarg.h (CodeSaathi extension)
learningObjectives: Explain the C concept and its rules.
Trace the example and describe data flow.
Identify relevant failure and boundary cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A variadic function accepts a fixed set of named parameters followed by a variable number of arguments, indicated by an ellipsis. The stdarg.h macros va_start, va_arg, va_copy and va_end access those additional arguments according to a convention established by the function.
understand.whyItMatters: Variadic interfaces are flexible but provide limited automatic type checking. The function needs a reliable way to know the number and types of supplied arguments, such as a count or format string.
understand.analogy: Treat the operation as a clearly specified contract between the program and its data.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's type, lifetime, I/O and object representation rules.

explain.narrative:
A variadic function accepts a fixed set of named parameters followed by a variable number of arguments, indicated by an ellipsis. The stdarg.h macros va_start, va_arg, va_copy and va_end access those additional arguments according to a convention established by the function.

Check all return values, object lifetimes, types and preconditions. Enable compiler warnings and test expected as well as failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: count tells the function how many int arguments follow. va_arg retrieves each as int. Passing an argument with a mismatched type or incorrect count can cause undefined behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the three va_arg operations and the running total.
practise.independentTask: Design a variadic function with a documented count and supported argument type. Explain how misuse is prevented or constrained.
hints: Always call va_end for a va_list after use.
Default argument promotions affect the types retrieved from the variadic portion.
Variadic arguments do not carry runtime type metadata for automatic checking.
